profile.profile:
American singer, songwriter, pianist, composer, arranger and civil rights activist, born 21 February 1933 in Tryon, North Carolina, USA, died 21 April 2003 in Carry-le-Rouet, Bouches-du-Rhône, France (aged 70)

Nina was giving piano recitals after playing at her local church at an early age. Her childhood piano lessons were funded by her mother's employer and a local fund set up by her music teacher, so impressed were they by her talent.

She moved to Philadelphia aged 17, teaching piano and playing to raise the money for her studies at New York's renowned Juilliard School Of Music. To fund her family she worked in a bar in Atlantic City where she was also required to sing and built up a devoted following.

She recorded Gershwin's "I Loves You Porgy" which became a US Top 20 hit and transported her to a bigger stage, performing at [l280434] and the [l318621].

Her repertoire went on to embrace numerous civil rights anthems, a movement for which she was a passionate and prominent supporter. She left the US in the 1970s, moving first to Barbados, and some other places, including Africa and the Netherlands, before eventually settling in France where she died from cancer in 2003.

She won a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award in 2017 and was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2018.

Mother of [a1559889].

profile.profile:
Alternative / modern rock band from Madison, Wisconsin, USA.

Shirley Manson - vocals, keyboards, guitar
Duke Erikson - bass, guitar, keyboards
Steve Marker - guitar, keyboards, loops
Butch Vig - drums, loops, noise, fx

In the early 1980s, rock producers Vig (Nirvana, Smashing Pumpkins) and Marker founded Smart Studios, a recording studio in Madison, Wisconsin. Vig and musician friend Erikson formed the group Fire Town in the late 1980s, an offshoot from their disbanded band Spooner. Marker was their roadie. Vig and Marker began making electronic/rock mixes for artists like Nine Inch Nails and House Of Pain. In 1993 they decided they wanted to form a band that employed the remix and genre-bending approach they experimented with earlier and began looking for a singer and fourth collaborator. Guitarist Steve Marker came across a video of Scottish band Angelfish on MTV's "120 Minutes". Struck by the lead singer's (Shirley Manson) voice, he informed the guys and their manager contacted Manson, inviting her to audition in Madison, Wisconsin. After an unsuccessful audition, Manson asked to audition again, which led to skeletal versions of a few songs. The band officially formed in 1994, and released their self-titled debut in 1995. All four members are involved in songwriting and production.

Calloway's orchestra rotated as a 'house band' with that of [a145257] at the famous Cotton Club in Harlem through the Prohibition era. His snappy 'zoot-suit' dress sense and skillful vaudeville song-and-dance routines made him a popular entertainer. His 'moonwalking' predating that of Michael Jackson by about a half-century.
In later years, he continued performing and featured in films, such as "The Cincinnati Kid" (1965) with Steve McQueen and Edward G. Robinson. The "Cab Calloway School of the Arts", in Wilmington, Delaware, was dedicated in his name in 1994. Calloway died shortly after a stroke and his ashes are interred at Ferncliffe Cemetery in Hartsdale, New York.

profile.profile:
Latin rock band from San Francisco, California, USA, led by guitarist [a=Carlos Santana]. The band was formed in 1966 under the name Santana Blues Band. In 1967, the band changed its name to Santana. They debuted as Santana at [a=Bill Graham]'s Fillmore West theater in San Francisco on June 16, 1968. Steered on by Graham, they first came to a wider public attention after their performance at the Woodstock Festival in 1969. This initial exposure made their first three albums hits at the time, all with Columbia, the first record company that signed the band. By 1972 / 1973 however, there were rifts in the band and two of its members left to form [a=Journey].

Caravanserai from 1972 marked the start of a new, more jazz oriented chapter in Santana's career, as the band now moved away from rock and towards a more experimental and complex sound. The triple live album Lotus concludes that period. Over the next decades, line-up changes were common, the music at times evolved more commercially and pop oriented although never losing the initial latin influence. 

Santana left Columbia in 1991 and signed with Polydor for their 1992's Milagro album and the subsequent releases, until Clive Davis signed the group to Arista in 1998, with whom they achieved their greatest commercial and critical success: so far, Santana has won a total of 8 Grammy Awards and 3 Latin Grammy Awards which were all awarded in 2000 for the 1999 Supernatural album (which also earned them their first No. 1 hit Smooth).

In 1994, Santana played at the commemorative concert at Woodstock, 25 years after the band's transformative performance at the original festival. In 1998, the group was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, with Carlos Santana, Jose Chepito Areas, David Brown, Mike Carabello, Gregg Rolie, and Michael Shrieve being honored. In 2016 they released [m986309], a studio album that reunites the early ’70s lineup and signifies the first time in 45 years - since 1971’s multi-platinum classic Santana III - that the quintet has recorded together. Santana again played at Bethel New York for the Woodstock 50th anniversary.

The 2010 released Guitar Heaven collection of classic rock covers turned out to be their last album for Arista. 2012's Shape Shifter was released on their Sony-distributed imprint Starfaith. With 2014's Corazón, Santana surpassed the Rolling Stones and is one of only two music acts in Billboard history to score at least one Top Ten album for 6 consecutive decades from the 1960s on. Santana has signed with Concord since 2018 and has released the Narada Michael Walden-produced EP In Search Of The Mona Lisa and the Rick Rubin produced full-length album Africa Speaks in 2019.

British electronic label. 

Founded by [a=Steve Beckett], [a=Rob Mitchell (7)] (RIP 2001), and [a=Robert Gordon], Warp (originally to be named Warped, but shortened for communication ease, and later expanded by the backronym "[b]W[/b]e [b]A[/b]re [b]R[/b]easonable [b]P[/b]eople"), is one of the world's most respected, influential, and loved electronic/experimental dance labels. After many years in Sheffield, UK, they later moved to and are based in London, UK. 

Bleep.com, Warp's digital music sales site, was also pioneering in being amongst the first to provide high-quality variable bit rate MP3s for sale (later FLAC and other lossless formats). It joined a slew of attempts at selling music online, and included exclusive tracks, samplings of forthcoming albums, and rarities. 

UK label, label code: LC 2070 / LC 02070. 

Related labels: 
[l=Warp Records Limited] - a Warp company, incorporated in 25 February 1993, and used for some copyright credits. 
[l=Warp Music] / [l=Warp Music Publishing] - publishing companies associated with Warp. 
[l=Lex Records] - former Warp sub-label. 
[l=Arcola] - Warp abstract dance-oriented sub-label. 
[l=LuckyMe] / [l=Night Slugs] - Warp partner labels. 

In winter 2005, the book "Warp" by Rob Young was released as the first volume in the "Labels Unlimited" series. It gives a fully illustrated overview of the label's history and also confirms the following gaps in the cat#'s, though with some mistakes: 

[i][u]Albums:[/u] 
WARP 13 / WARP 99 / WARP 113 - no releases. 
WARP 93 - Priest "Untitled" (unreleased). 
WARP 109 - [a=Squarepusher] "Budakhan Maximized" (unreleased). 
WARP 118 - [a=Chris Morris] "Blue Jam II" (unreleased). 

[u]Singles:[/u] 
WAP 13 - supposedly unreleased, but some copies of WARP LP 1 were pressed with this cat#. 
WAP 30 - flyer for WARP Party at the Leadmill, Sheffield, Fri 8 Jan 1993. 
WAP 85 - is given to [a=Jimi Tenor] "[m=43418]" but was never used, as it was actually released by Rough Trade Germany with no Warp cat# on the release. 
WAP 99 - unique set of artwork by [l=The Designers Republic] (tDR). 
WAP 113 / WAP 131 / WAP 143 / WAP 148 - no releases. [/i] 

NOTE: Many Warp releases were licensed to record labels outside the UK. Some of these releases include a Warp cat# as well as their own. These labels include: 
- [l=Indisc] - usually uses the Warp cat# with an [b]extra 107[/b] before the number in addition to the Indisc cat#. Sometimes it uses just a Warp cat#. 
- [l=Rough Trade Records GmbH] which later became [l=Zomba Records] - uses the Warp cat# on releases that use the Warp label code in addition to the RTD 126.XXXX.X cat#. Prior to this when the releases featured the RTD/Zomba label code (LC 5661) the Warp cat# did not appear.
